claims.statement: The first-mark identity and cover-loss inequality give a sound conditional reduction of the pointwise leaf sign to residual shadow or matching-sign hypotheses. Under the stated parent cover bound, the matching-size threshold follows from cover loss, but each d>=3 residual also requires the separate rank condition p-2>=K(d). The s=5 Catalan estimate has zero empty-fiber margin and a negative first nonempty-fiber floor at q=p-2, so it does not force the parent cover bound.
claims.scope: Conditional marked-forest and leaf-deletion shell reduction only, retaining inherited residual matching-sign applications at their exact hypotheses. It does not prove the cover or rank premises for all eligible trees and does not resolve the registered favorable-leaf aggregate.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: The partition, cover-loss arithmetic, ordinary-shadow boundary, and s=5 cutoff check out. The unconditional shell and aggregate conclusions remain unsupported because the parent cover threshold and residual rank gates are not established generally; the matching theorems remain inherited applications.

limitations: The cover and rank hypotheses are conditional and are not proved for every eligible tree.
Residual matching-sign results are inherited and are used only under their stated matching-size and rank conditions.
No exhaustive tree census or source replay was performed; no counterexample is claimed.
The s=5 computation shows failure of this cover-Catalan bound, not failure of the shell assertion.
The favorable-leaf aggregate remains unresolved by this claim.
